info.name: Readr v2 API — Contract Tests
info.description:
This Postman collection validates the backend API contract for the Readr v2 application.

Endpoints covered:

- Health (service availability)
    
- Auth
    
- Books CRUD
    
- Sessions CRUD
    
- Backup
    

The tests verify:

- endpoint behavior
    
- request validation
    
- response schemas
    
- deterministic ordering
    
- error handling
    

These requests are used during development to confirm that backend behavior matches the expected frontend contract before integration.

Test environments assume:

baseUrl = [http://localhost:4000](http://localhost:4000)

other API requests. If this request fails, the rest of the test suite  
should not be run.

item.name: Sessions

exec: pm.test("Each returned session has required fields", function () {

request.description:
Returns all reading sessions currently stored in the system.

The endpoint supports filtering and pagination through query parameters  
such as bookId, date ranges, limit, and offset.

Results are returned in deterministic order:

1. date DESC
    
2. createdAt DESC
    
3. id DESC
    

Endpoint  
GET /api/sessions

Creates a new reading session using pages as the reading metric.

This request also serves as the main lifecycle seed for the Sessions folder.  
The returned id is stored in the Postman collection variable createdSessionId  
so that subsequent GET, PATCH, and DELETE requests can run automatically.

Endpoint  
POST /api/sessions

Creates a new reading session using minutes as the reading metric.

This verifies that the Sessions API accepts a valid payload when only minutes  
are provided and pages are omitted.

Endpoint  
POST /api/sessions

Creates a new reading session with both pages and minutes provided.

This verifies that the Sessions API accepts and stores both supported reading  
metrics in the same session.

Endpoint  
POST /api/sessions

Attempts to create an invalid reading session.

This test confirms that the Sessions API enforces the rule requiring at least  
one reading metric and returns a validation error for invalid payloads.

Expected result: HTTP 400 validation error.

Endpoint  
POST /api/sessions

exec: pm.test("Invalid book id format is rejected", function () {

item.name: 7. Create Session — valid id format, nonexistent book

request.description:
Attempts to create a reading session using a syntactically valid book id that  
does not exist in the database.

This verifies that the API correctly distinguishes between malformed ids and  
well-formed ids that fail resource lookup.

Endpoint  
POST /api/sessions

Retrieves the session created during the main lifecycle flow.

This request uses the createdSessionId collection variable populated by the  
pages-only create request and verifies that the resource can be retrieved  
successfully by id.

Endpoint  
GET /api/sessions/:id

Updates only the notes field for the session created during the lifecycle flow.

This verifies that partial updates work correctly without changing unrelated  
fields on the session.

Endpoint  
PATCH /api/sessions/:id

exec: pm.test("Minutes remain unchanged or null", function () {

request.description:
Updates only the pages field for the session created during the lifecycle flow.

This verifies that numeric reading metrics can be updated independently and  
that other fields remain intact.

Endpoint  
PATCH /api/sessions/:id

Updates the session by clearing pages while keeping minutes present.

This verifies that the merged PATCH validation allows one reading metric to be  
cleared as long as the session still retains at least one valid metric.

Endpoint  
PATCH /api/sessions/:id

item.name: 13. Session — set pages to null, keep minutes

exec: pm.test("Pages cleared and minutes preserved", function () {

request.description:
Updates the session by clearing pages while keeping minutes present.

This verifies that the merged PATCH validation allows one reading metric to be  
cleared as long as the session still retains at least one valid metric.

Endpoint  
PATCH /api/sessions/:id

Attempts to update a session with an empty request body.

This verifies that the API rejects empty PATCH requests and requires at least  
one field to be provided for update operations.

Endpoint  
PATCH /api/sessions/:id

Attempts to update a session so that both pages and minutes become null.

This verifies that merged PATCH validation prevents a session from being left  
without any valid reading metric.

Endpoint  
PATCH /api/sessions/:id

request.description:

returns only matching records.

 ```

exec: pm.test("Results are within date range", function () {

request.description:
Filters sessions using inclusive date range query parameters.

This verifies that the from and to query parameters are parsed correctly and  
that the returned sessions fall within the expected range.

Endpoint:

```
GET /api/sessions?from=<date>&to=<date>

 ```

The API should reject this request with a validation error.

Endpoint:

```

 ```

 ```
